title: The most detailed pictures of the Sun… EVER
description:
Scientists have snapped some shiny new pictures of the Sun in the most detail we’ve ever seen. They used a super powerful solar telescope to show "whirlpools" of activity which are the Sun’s magnetic field being twisted and moved by the motion of hot gas.

Victoria Gill, our Science Correspondent chats to us about how the pictures were taken by the Inouye Solar Telescope and what they tell us about the universe.

Plus, we hear from three space photography enthusiasts and science content creators.

summaryZh: 本集 BBC 節目《What in the World》探討由夏威夷 Daniel K. Inouye 太陽望遠鏡拍攝到的史上最詳細太陽照片。BBC 科學記者 Victoria Gill 解釋，影像呈現的漩渦圖案與 Kelvin-Helmholtz 不穩定性，展示了熱氣體如何拖曳太陽磁場並輸送能量。此動態過程加熱了太陽外層大氣（日冕），並引發日冕物質拋射，產生極光與太空天氣，進而影響地球的衛星、 GPS 與通訊。此外， 3 位太空攝影愛好者與科學創作者也分享了這些照片對宇宙探索及地球科技應用的意義。
summaryEn: In this episode of What in the World, host Hannah Gelbart and BBC Science Correspondent Victoria Gill discuss the highest-resolution images of the Sun ever captured, taken by the Daniel K. Inouye Solar Telescope in Hawaii. Gill explains how the high-detail images reveal swirling magnetic fields and Kelvin-Helmholtz instability, showing how energy moves from the Sun's surface to heat its outer atmosphere (corona). These magnetic dynamics drive solar flares and coronal mass ejections—phenomena that create auroras and space weather capable of disrupting satellites, GPS systems, and communications on Earth. The episode also features perspectives from three space photography enthusiasts and science communicators on how these astronomical breakthroughs advance fundamental physics and practical technologies.
